Court No. - 70
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 36813 of 2023

Applicant :- Manish Kumar
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others

Counsel for Applicant :- Kush Kumar Pandey,Dharamraj Singh
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.
Supplementary affidavit filed today on behalf of the applicant is taken on record.
2.  Sri Brijesh Pratap Singh, learned AGA for the State apprised the Court that on 11.08.2023 notice has been served to the informant of the case.
Despite service of notice, none appeared on behalf of the informant.

3. Heard Sri Ram Raksha Tiwari, Advocate, holding brief of Sri Kush Kumar Pandey, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Brijesh Pratap Singh, learned AGA for the State-respondent.
4.

The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No. 15 of 2023, under Sections 363, 366, 376 IPC & 5/6 POCSO Act, Police Station- Kheeri, District- Prayagraj, during pendency of the trial in the court below.

sentences.text: FIR of the present case was lodged on 09.02.2023 against applicant and four others and according to the FIR, on 08.11.2022, applicant and other accused persons committed rape upon daughter of the informant aged about 15 years and with regard to incident dated 08.11.2022, a FIR under Sections 363, 506 IPC could only be lodged due to the police officials, however, according to the informant, offence under Section 376 IPC is clearly made out against the applicant and others.

6. It is further mentioned in the FIR that on 21.11.2022, daughter of the informant was handed over to her and again on 25.11.2022, applicant and other accused persons abducted the victim and when FIR of the informant was not lodged then on 03.12.2022, she moved an application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. and thereafter FIR of the instant case was lodged on 09.02.2023.
7.
Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that on the basis of false allegation, applicant has been made accused in the present matter.

He further submitted that with regard to offence of rape dated 08.11.2022 a separate FIR was lodged by the informant but that FIR was lodged only under Sections 363, 506 IPC and after investigation, final report has been submitted in that case and this fact is evident from Annexure No. 1 to the supplementary affidavit.

8. He further submitted that as far as allegation with regard to present case is concerned, as per the allegation, on 25.11.2022 applicant and others abducted the victim, who was aged about 15 years but during investigation, when statement of the victim was recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. then she categorically stated that her family members tortured her and due torture of her parents, she herself has left her house and she did not make any allegation against the applicant and in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. she stated that she had already performed marriage with the applicant and she herself had gone alongwith the applicant, therefore, there are material contradictions in both the statements of the victim.

9. He further submitted that however, as per the school record, at the time of incident, victim was about 16 year's old but in fact, she was major aged about 18 years and even appearance wise, she looked like major and intentionally her ossification test was not conducted during investigation.
10. He further submitted that applicant is not having any criminal history and he is in jail since 08.06.2023.
11. Per contra, learned AGA although, opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the argument on facts advanced by learned counsel for the applicant.
12. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

13. From the perusal of the FIR of the present case, it appears that two set of incident have been mentioned in it and with regard to incident dated 08.11.2022, it appears that a separate FIR was lodged against the applicant and others in case crime number-288 of 2022 and as per the S.A.-1,
after investigation, final report has been submitted in that case.

sentences.text: Further, as far as allegation with regard to present case is concerned, as per the allegation, on 25.11.2022 applicant and other accused persons abducted the victim, aged about 15 years but from the statements of the victim recorded during investigation, allegation levelled against the applicant in the FIR appears to be false.

Victim in her statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C.
categorically stated that due to bad behaviour of her parents, she left her paternal home and she even did not disclose the name of the applicant and when her statement was recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. then she stated that she has already performed marriage with the applicant and she had gone along with the applicant according to her own wish, therefore, I find force in the argument advanced by learned counsel for the applicant that there are material contradictions in both the statements of the victim recorded during investigation.

15. Therefore, considering the material contradictions in both the statements of the victim recorded during investigation and the fact that applicant is not having any criminal history and is in custody for last about six months, in my view applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
16. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

17. Let the applicant- Manish Kumar be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
18. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

19. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
Order Date :- 15.12.2023
